title: Welcome to Japan, Ms. Elf!
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Salaryman Kazuhiro Kitase has visited a fantasy world in his dreams since childhood. When he and his elf companion Marie are killed by a dragon there, she wakes up beside him in modern Japan, and the two begin traveling back and forth. Marie discovers Japanese food and daily life, while quests in the other world continue and others, including the dragon Wridra, come to visit.
life_message: Curiosity, shared meals and friendship across worlds make ordinary life feel like an adventure.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Conflicts with the dragon are settled by offering food and drink, not revenge.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Kazuhiro and Marie roam freely between worlds and choose their own adventures.

Civic vs kin.evidence: A found circle of companions and neighbors rather than family duty.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Companions are equals; the ancient dragon joins as a friend.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Modern Japan meets a magical world; neither side's ways are imposed.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Leisure, food and exploration are the focus; Kazuhiro keeps his day job.

folkways.japan: The series showcases everyday Japanese food, neighborhoods and salaryman routine through a newcomer's eyes, a common device for presenting ordinary Japanese life as delightful.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewer (via Wikipedia) found the story largely uneventful; summaries show a slice-of-life tone with no stated moral (to verify).
delivery.note: Summaries describe a relaxed slice-of-life story whose values come through shared meals and travel rather than argument.

winners_losers: Friendship and curiosity win; the jealous mage who tries to thwart the pair is the main antagonist.
